cursor.note: PROVED. THE DEFECT, in one sentence a year from now will still parse: setsid detaches a terminal and does nothing whatever to a cgroup, so the ground loop the launcher started lived inside the session's own scope and died with the window. Measured before the fix, not suspected — the kernel reported ONE cgroup string for both loop and caller, and the beat counter froze at 1 the instant the caller's tree was killed. THE FIX: a transient user unit via systemd-run --user, so the process is forked and owned by the manager. THE PREDICATE THAT MAKES IT CHECKABLE, and the part worth carrying to other problems: a '.scope' is a cgroup built AROUND processes someone else forked, so its lifetime is the forker's; a '.service' is one the manager forked and owns. Green is 'service', red is 'scope'. That is why the probe needs no list of what counts as a terminal — konsole, tmux, sshd, and whatever ships next all fall out of the second clause without ever being named, and the watch cannot go stale against a terminal nobody thought of. The chart raised the enumeration problem as an open unknown; it dissolved rather than being solved. THREE THINGS THE SHAPE COSTS, each non-obvious and each now in the charter: SuccessExitStatus=3 because the singleton guard's loser exits 3 BY DESIGN and a nonzero exit leaves a transient unit loaded in 'failed', holding its own name against every later launch; --setenv=HOME and --setenv=PATH because systemd-run hands the unit the MANAGER's environment, not the caller's, and a PATH without ~/.cairn/venv/bin is a loop that cannot import itself; and a HELD NAME must never fall through to the setsid spawn, because that spawn would be a second claimant racing the first (ticket the-beater-holds-the-claim). Only an UNREACHABLE systemd is a fall-through. RESHAPED MID-BUILD BY ITS OWN COST MEASUREMENT. The ticket's falsifier lists DELAY as wrong intent, so the first working draft's three round trips to the manager were attacked down to one. The liveness probe is gone because THE START ATTEMPT IS THE PROBE — and that is the stricter test, not merely the cheaper one: the old shape committed to the systemd path the moment its proxy passed, and a start that then failed left the launch with no loop at all. reset-failed moved to the retry, where the state it clears actually exists. Cost, n=15, arms INTERLEAVED, real launcher driven to exec: setsid 76.1ms median, unit 118.0ms. ~42ms, recorded WITHOUT a gate because one reading is not a threshold. NON-HOLLOW: red first at 16:23 against the unmodified tree at 124442b — exactly 5 of 24 arms failing, the 19 passing including all five prime-directive arms — then green four times, sealed twice under the tester in netns. The kill is a CGROUP kill, not the killpg the chart's own instrument specified: setsid has already left the process group, so a killpg would spare the loop wherever it lived and buy a green that means nothing. FOUR FINDINGS ABOUT THE INSTRUMENTS RATHER THAN THE BUILD, kept because the next voyage inherits them: criterion 1 named the wrong weapon (killpg) for its own claim; criterion 7's grep cannot tell a mention from a read and returns 10 hits for 1 reader; criterion 6 assumed the probe's smoke surface took a pid when it silently ignored one, so the reading it asked for was not performable as written; and a cost harness leaked 14 orphaned loops into this session by cleaning up with 'systemctl stop <unit>' while its own control arm had no unit — the leak then loaded the machine and inflated the very numbers being measured. AND THE CROSSING WAS REFUSED ONCE ON THE WAY HERE, by the build gate, on a defect this voyage did not create: launchers/probes/reported_but_unfixed_floor.py spelled the instance root by hand. Fixed, not triaged — Law 9 has no pre-existing clause. It composes address.resolve now; log_path() is deliberately NOT what it uses, because that indexes by device and 'boot' is the machine's own trail. THE WATCH STANDS AND IS NOT RETIRED BY THIS VOYAGE. The live fire drove the real launcher with a stand-in that exits at once, so outlived_its_spawner came back True against a 70-second-old loop — the FIXTURE meeting 'enough', not a caller dying. The ticket ruled on this in advance: enough is 'at least one caller die while the loop kept beating'. In production the spawner IS the claude session, via exec, and it lives for hours. What the watch is waiting for is a real session's death. TWO DOORS REFUSED THIS CROSSING AND BOTH WERE RIGHT. (1) The harbor's clearance gate: launchers' charter declared its owner only in prose — 'Akien owns the launch contract; CC drafts' — and prose cannot gate, because matching an actor against a 60-character English sentence is a substring scan that goes green for the wrong reason. Added gated_by ['Akien','CC'], which is a TRANSLATION of the sentence already on file and not a new grant, with the reason beside it; recompile gate poked in the same act. (2) Then the seal, correctly: the charter and probe edits moved the source under the proof, so the horizon closed (fingerprint d894ee3b -> 40ccd53c) and the harbor refused to clear onto code that was no longer the code that was proved. Re-ran and re-sealed green at the new fingerprint. That is Law 3 doing exactly its job on my own edits, and it caught them inside the same minute.

The spawn is parented on the CALLER'S cgroup: setsid detaches the tty and not the cgroup, so the one resident process in the system dies with whatever window launched it — measured twice (2026-08-10 reboot, 2026-08-18 Konsole scope oom-kill). It becomes a transient user unit (systemd-run --user --unit), a SIBLING of the caller's scope, guarded by the same probe+fall-through shape the memory scope 60 lines below already uses. MEASURED AT CHART AND IT CHANGED THE BUILD: a transient unit that exits NONZERO stays loaded in `failed` state and blocks its own name, and the singleton loser exits 3 BY DESIGN — so the naive change would wedge the unit name on the first losing launch and every later launch would silently fail to start the loop. SuccessExitStatus=3 plus a blind reset-failed (measured harmless on a live unit) close it. Chart chain: seven berths, validate at /home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/validate-20260818T160010-a6527557b941.json. The proof is written FIRST and run against the unmodified launcher, because a proof that has never seen the failure it grips is how a hollow green is bought.

window.note: PROVEME. launchers/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py — 24 arms, GREEN twice (16:38 and 16:41, 2026-08-18) against the shipped launcher, and RED FIRST: run at 16:23 against the UNMODIFIED launcher it failed on exactly the five arms the defect owns and passed the other fifteen, so the green is evidence about the world and not about the fixture. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS: before, the kernel put loop and caller in ONE cgroup (cairn-proof-caller-502361-1.scope for both) and the loop died with the caller's cgroup, beats frozen at 1; after, the loop sits in cairn-proof-loop-543825-1.service — kind 'service', lifetime 'manager' — and beats went 1 -> 2 ACROSS the kill of every pid in the caller's cgroup.procs. The kill is a cgroup kill, not a killpg, because setsid has already left the process group and a killpg would spare the loop and buy a hollow green. THE SPAWN WAS RESHAPED MID-BUILD BY ITS OWN COST MEASUREMENT: the first working draft asked the manager three questions per launch (a --scope liveness probe, a blind reset-failed, the start). The ticket's falsifier lists DELAY as wrong intent, so it was attacked: the probe is gone because THE START ATTEMPT IS THE PROBE — and that is the stricter test, not merely the cheaper one, since the old shape committed to the systemd path the moment the proxy passed and a start that then failed left the launch with no loop — and reset-failed moved to the retry, where the state it clears actually exists. The two failure modes are now kept apart: a HELD NAME retries once and then REFUSES, never falling through to a setsid spawn, because that spawn would be a second claimant racing the first (ticket the-beater-holds-the-claim); anything else means systemd is unreachable and the setsid fall-through is right. COST, MEASURED AND UNGATED (the validate berth asked for a reading, not a threshold): n=15 per arm, INTERLEAVED, launcher driven to exec — setsid 76.1ms median, unit 118.0ms. ~42ms. TWO METHOD FINDINGS TRAVEL WITH THAT NUMBER: sequential arms first reported one round trip as SLOWER than three (they were measuring the drift between the arms), and the first per-stage breakdown read 125ms of dbus where the same commands later read 30ms — the difference was load average 18.7 vs 3.5, and the 18.7 was 14 orphaned ground loops LEAKED BY THE MEASURING HARNESS itself, which cleaned up with `systemctl stop <unit>` while its control arm was a setsid with no unit to stop. Both harnesses now clean up by what the process IS (its HOME), not by a name one arm happened to use. TWO PROOF BUGS WERE FOUND BY THE RED AND FIXED BEFORE THE BUILD: the prime-directive arm pruned PATH of every directory holding systemd-run, which on this host is /usr/bin (and /bin, a symlink to it), leaving the launcher without `script` — isolation that removes the world reads exactly like the defect; it now builds a symlink directory withholding systemd-run alone and ASSERTS both halves. And the one-reader census counted a bash one-liner inside the memory-scope proof's stand-in as a second reader; it now counts python reads (exactly one, the probe) and declares every other mention by name with its reason, with a staleness check so a dead exemption reds too. Charter delta at launchers/intention+why.json superclaude.ground_loop_spawn — rewritten for the one-round-trip design, the superseded why_the_blind_reset_failed key REMOVED rather than left standing beside its replacement; recompile gate poked in the same act (exit 0).

window.note: WATCHME(the_heartbeat_outlives_its_caller). Probe ARMED at the berth the ticket names, cairn/devices/ground_loop/probes/does_the_heartbeat_outlive_its_caller.py, module-level PROBE carrying both a carry and an enough. THE PREDICATE TAKES NO LIST, and that is the answer to the enumeration problem raised at hypothesize: green is a '.service' (a unit the user manager forked and OWNS) and red is a '.scope' (a cgroup built AROUND processes someone else forked, so its lifetime is the forker's). Every terminal — konsole, vte, tmux, sshd, named or unnamed, and whatever ships next — falls out of the second clause without ever being listed. The watch cannot go stale against a terminal nobody thought of, because it was never asking about terminals. READ LIVE AGAINST TWO PIDS at 16:52 on 2026-08-18: the launcher-started loop 574986 GREEN (cairn-ground-loop.service, lifetime 'manager'), and this session's own shell RED (superclaude-350050.scope, lifetime 'caller') — the negative arm run against a real process in a real terminal scope, not a fixture. THE SMOKE SURFACE WAS DEFECTIVE AND IS FIXED IN THE SAME ACT. Its __main__ accepted a pid argument and IGNORED it: two runs against different pids came back byte-identical, under a heading that read like an answer about the pid asked. That is a diagnostic surface answering a question it was not asked (Law 7), and it is the failure mode that would have made every future hand-check of this watch worthless while looking like it worked. It now honours the argument and echoes it back as pid_asked_about, so the reading names its own subject. AND THE FIRST CLEARANCE DOES NOT COUNT — recorded here because the evidence LOOKS like it should. The live fire drove the real launcher with a stand-in binary that exits immediately, so the spawner (574929) was gone within seconds and outlived_its_spawner came back True against a loop only 70 seconds old. That was the FIXTURE satisfying 'enough', not a caller dying. In production the spawner pid IS the claude session, via exec, and it lives for hours. The ticket's spec already ruled on this in advance — 'NOT satisfied by the launch that installs it... Enough when it has seen at least one caller die while the loop kept beating' — and the probe's docstring had claimed a DIFFERENT reason for standing (that the live loop was placed in its unit by hand), which the live fire made false the moment the launcher started the loop itself. The docstring now says the spec's reason. THE WATCH STANDS, and what it is waiting for is a real session's death.
